newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki drifts lower in meagre volume.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki drifts lower in meagre volume.

text.p: Shares drifted to a lower close in meagre volume on Tuesday, with many investors sidelined ahead of Nokia's half-year report next Monday and with more inactivity expected this week, operators said.
The FOX portfolio index fell 0.35 percent to 1,213.47, while the all-share HEX index edged down 0.14 percent to 3,524.90 points. Volume was a modest 415 million.
"Everyone is just waiting," one market analyst said, "I don't see much happening in Nokia's share price this week ... it's hard to see where the market can get a direction from."
Banking group Merita dragged the index, falling 0.50 markka to 23.30. Volume in Merita was a modest 25 million markka, though it accounted for six percent of bourse turnover.
"Some of the heavy buyers in Merita last week are now out of the market," one analyst said.
Nokia A ended up 0.80 markka at 449.00 after trading in a narrow 447.00-450.00 markka range all day. The less-traded Nokia K share closed off 1.50 markka at 447.50.

Sporting goods group Amer caused a ripple of activity on the otherwise quiet bourse. It closed up 4.70 markka at 96.00 markka, after jumping briefly to 100.00 on news that it would redeem 275,000 of its K shares that had been offered to a British investor.
Trade in Amer was fairly lively, with volume rising above 40 million markka in less than half a session after trade in the share had been suspended for the morning pending the news.

"It was positive news, and the share reacted immediately," one broker said of Amer's move to exercise its right to redeem the K shares that had been sold to Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne, and to combine its A and K share series.
After the news, equities analysts said they saw upside for Amer, though one said the share would run into firm resistance at around 99.00-100.00 markka.
